title: Demand Fairness Orchestrator and Commitment Simulator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: We receive concentrated inbound requests from ~20 key accounts that require preferential handling (escalations, dedicated scope lanes, and release guarantees). Current intake is manual and baked into tactical PM/AE judgment; this leads to inconsistent outcomes, perceived unfairness across accounts, and occasional SLA misses.

Goal: Build a 'Demand Fairness Orchestrator' — a policy-driven simulation and allocation engine that helps PMs and sales leaders: 1) quantify fair allocation of roadmap capacity across top accounts, 2) simulate commitment decisions (timebox vs. scope fractioning), and 3) surface trade-offs (latency to delivery, revenue delta, and risk).

Proposed approach:
- Intake signals: combine weighted account signals (ARR, strategic tier, legal deadlines, support severity, churn risk, partner mandates) plus product-level constraints (capacity budget, critical SLOs).
- Policy primitives: fairness constraints (proportional, floor/ceiling guarantees, entropy-regularized allocation), urgency multipliers, and guarded exceptions for compliance or legal commitments.
- Simulator: deterministic and stochastic runs to show best/worst-case delivery dates, partial-scope bundles, and fallback rollouts. Includes a UI mock to run scenarios and export an 'allocation plan' that maps features -> account slices -> release windows.
- Integration points: ingest Top Account list from SFDC via data infra (ENG-21431), connect to roadmap capacity model (ENG-21432), persist plans to Confluence and issue-generation in Linear for accepted allocations.

Success metrics (first 6 weeks):
- Simulation adoption: 6 PMs + 3 AE leads run scenario at least once per planning cycle.
- Decision clarity: reduce manual escalation meetings by 30% (tracked in calendar invites).
- Predictability: 25% reduction in scope-change SLA misses for top accounts during pilot cohort.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Revenue-optimal allocations may conflict with fairness primitives; we will expose objective function sliders rather than hard defaults.
- Data freshness: some signals (churn risk) will be estimated; simulation will surface uncertainty bands.

Deliverables:
1) Specification doc + weighting defaults (Confluence link below).
2) Prototype simulator UI (Figma mock + lightweight web runner).
3) Integration tickets to wire data sources and emit allocation plans into Linear.

Notes: this is intentionally product-facing (PM-owned) with engineering delivering infra connectors. We will run the pilot with 10 lighthouse accounts before any org-wide rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc published with recommended weighting defaults and policy primitives
Prototype simulator supports running deterministic and stochastic scenarios with exportable allocation plan
End-to-end data pipeline ingest for Top Account signals (mock data accepted for pilot)
At least two planning cycles where the simulator is used to approve allocation plans for pilot accounts
Generated Linear tickets for accepted allocations (automated or manual import)
